title: Federated recovery choices and proofkit for tenant replay
content:
Purpose
This is a customer-facing draft combining a concise status update suitable for a status page entry plus an attached, plain-language post-incident summary and self-serve replay/proof kit for affected tenants. Draft is intentionally procedural and includes options customers can choose — we want clear decisions, not technical noise.

Audience
Primary: product and platform engineers at affected tenants, integration owners, and assigned customer success managers. Secondary: internal GTM and legal for sign-off.

TL;DR (one paragraph)
On 2026-09-28 21:14 UTC we observed a propagation bug in our federated routing layer that caused sporadic duplication and mis-ordering of responses for a subset of streaming sessions and batch inference jobs in eu-west-1. Impact window ~21:14–22:05 UTC. Most customers saw transient mis-ordering or duplicate partial outputs; a small percentage (0.6% of tenant requests during window) saw complete response duplication. We implemented a routing rollback and cache eviction at 21:44 UTC and completed integrity verification and tenant replay tooling by 22:05 UTC. Recommended customer actions below. We are offering a replay evidence package and manual reconciliation assistance where needed.

Status page blurb (concise, for posting)
Title: Partial response duplication / mis-ordering — eu-west-1 (resolved)
Status: Resolved
Summary: A routing regression caused occasional duplicated or mis-ordered tokens for some streaming and batch calls in eu-west-1 between 2026-09-28 21:14 UTC and 22:05 UTC. We applied a rollback and completed integrity checks; no customer data was exfiltrated. If you observed duplicate or inconsistent outputs, follow the provided self-serve replay instructions or contact your CSM for assisted reconciliation.
Affected services: Hosted API (generation, streaming), Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 using federated routing
Customer impact: Possible duplicate partial or full responses; application-level idempotency may surface duplicates
Post-incident action: Full postmortem available; replay evidence package available to affected tenants.

Customer-facing post-incident summary (longer)
1) What happened (plain language)
- We deploy a multi-region routing layer that assigns requests to serving capacity based on capacity and latency policies. A recent change to session handoff logic caused a race when stream continuations were routed between nodes. In some continuations the streaming buffer was replayed unintentionally, producing duplicated tokens or slight re-ordering. This occurred only when a session was mid-TTL and routed across nodes within the same region.
- Root cause: an ordering invariant was not enforced when applying an in-flight KV cache merge during a handoff. The regression was introduced by a routing optimization (PR #2946) that aimed to reduce tail latency.
- Failure mode: duplicate partial responses, occasional full response replay in the client session history. No response truncation or model-state corruption observed.

2) Who was affected
- A minority subset of live streaming sessions and batch jobs in eu-west-1 between 21:14–22:05 UTC on 2026-09-28.
- Internal metrics: ~0.6% of tenant requests during window produced duplicated complete responses; ~2.3% produced partial token duplication or ordering anomalies.
- Customers who pin to specific dedicated nodes without session affinity were disproportionately affected.

3) What we did (step-by-step timeline, short bullets)
- 21:14 UTC — anomaly alerted by streaming integrity monitors (token reorder spikes).
- 21:19 UTC — Triage: identified recent routing optimization rollout as common factor (canary logs).
- 21:24 UTC — scoped affected request classes and tenants; compiled initial list for outreach.
- 21:30 UTC — applied targeted throttling to federated handoff decisions to reduce surface area.
- 21:44 UTC — rolled back routing optimization and forced graceful session drains; initiated cache eviction on flagged nodes.
- 21:52 UTC — began replay/integrity verification on queued artifacts; started building tenant-specific evidence packages.
- 22:05 UTC — verification complete for majority; service fully nominal.
- 22:10 UTC — status page updated, CSM outreach started for top-affected customers.

4) What impact means for your product (concise guidance)
- Streaming clients: you may have received repeated token fragments or brief re-ordering. Recommended: detect and drop identical contiguous tokens on client-side or re-request in idempotent flows. We include a sample client-side idempotency snippet in the proofkit.
- Batch jobs: some outputs may contain duplicate lines/records. Recommended: run a dedupe pass (hash-based) when replaying.
- Audit logs: request IDs remain unique; duplicates are identifiable by identical payload + timestamp clusters — our evidence package will include per-request checksums.

5) Self-serve recovery choices (what tenants can do now)
Option A — Automated replay (recommended for most):
- Use the provided replay API to re-run affected requests against verified model snapshot. This API accepts a request batch ID and returns deduplicated outputs plus an integrity manifest.
- Expected time: minutes — depends on tenant volume.
Option B — Manual reconciliation (for teams needing fine control):
- Download the evidence package and run local dedupe/merge scripts included in the kit.
- We provide example scripts for node/python/Go.
Option C — Assisted replay by Redwood:
- For customers who prefer us to run the replay and provide an attested replay manifest we will schedule a run and provide a signed artifact and reconciliation notes. Priority scheduling available for customers with SLA contracts.

6) Proof kit contents (what we'll deliver)
- Per-request integrity manifest (request_id, timestamp, checksum, serving_node_id)
- Concise replay script and instructions (node/python/Go) tuned for the most common SDK versions
- Sample dedupe filters and idempotency heuristics
- Evidence package (compressed logs limited to request identifiers and non-sensitive metadata)
- Optional signed attestation if you request assisted replay

7) Customer instructions — quickstart (step-by-step for option A)
- Step 1: Identify impacted request_batch_id(s) from your logs or use our relationship table (we included a CSV mapping in the evidence package).
- Step 2: Call POST /internal/tenant-replay with body {"tenant_id":"<id>", "batch_id":"<batch_id>", "mode":"deduped"} (note: endpoint is for audit/replay only; we will provide a short-lived API key in the evidence package).
- Step 3: Receive archive with deduplicated outputs + integrity-manifest.json. Validate checksums against your copy.
- Step 4: Apply outputs to your downstream pipeline; run unit tests where applicable.

8) Compensation and SLA notes
- We are offering a one-time credit equal to 2x the request units associated with the affected window to tenants who opt for replay or who show material downstream customer-facing impact.
- For customers under Dedicated contracts with explicit SLAs, we are opening a formal SLO exception review and will expedite manual reconciliation at no extra cost.

9) Preventive actions (what we're changing)
- Reverted the optimization and re-added strict ordering invariant checks in the routing handoff path.
- Extended streaming integrity monitors and synthetic session tests covering cross-node handoffs.
- Added a canary gating step for routing changes that includes a small cross-node shuffle test.
- Adding a post-deploy quick-scan that rebuilds per-session token hashes for a rolling sample to detect regressions earlier.

10) How we’ll communicate ongoing progress
- Status page: final closure notice + link to this summary (within 24 hours).
- Direct CSM outreach: within 4 hours of this note for top-affected customers; scheduled follow-ups for others.
- Engineering postmortem: internal Confluence link will be shared once internal RCA slides are complete (ETA 72 hours).

FAQs (short)
Q: Was customer data exposed?
A: No. The issue caused duplicated token emission and ordering anomalies only; no exfiltration of customer data. Logs in evidence package exclude PII and sensitive payloads.
Q: Can this happen again?
A: Root cause fixes and additional monitors make recurrence unlikely; we also added canary tests to catch similar regressions in future deploys.
Q: Do I need to rotate keys or tokens?
A: No. This incident did not compromise credentials.

Open questions / notes-to-self (internal)
- Decide final credit/compensation margin with finance/legal before publishing (Maya to confirm) — leave placeholder in external copy until approved.
- Attach attestation template and short-lived replay key creation flow (secops sign-off required).
- Confirm which customers will be offered assisted replay proactively vs. on-request.

CSM outreach template (short)
Subject: Incident recap + replay kit available — action recommended
Hi <CustomerName>,
We detected and resolved a routing regression that caused occasional duplicate or mis-ordered responses for some requests in eu-west-1 on 2026-09-28. We’ve built a replay/evidence package for you that you can run yourself or ask us to run. Next steps:
- Please reply if you want Redwood to run the replay (we’ll need a point-of-contact and approval).
- If you prefer self-serve, we’ll upload the evidence package to the tenant folder and drop the short-lived replay key.
Thanks,
Aisha and the Customer Success team

Contact/Support
- Primary CSM: <assigned CSM name>
- For immediate technical assistance and assisted replay: cs-incident@redwood.ai (internal routing to on-call)
- Incident Jira: INF-5137

Appendix: quick internal checklist before publishing externally
- [ ] Legal/Finance compensation language approved (Maya)
- [ ] SecOps attestation template attached (Ethan)
- [ ] Evidence package uploaded to tenant folder for top-affected customers
- [ ] Statuspage entry scheduled and staged
- [ ] CSM outreach matrix created and assigned

-- end of draft --

Notes on tone: Keep external copy concise and non-technical but include clear choices and low-friction self-serve path. Internal checklist must be completed before we publish final verbiage that mentions credits/compensation.
